name: Halversen Longline Overcoat
description:
Halversen is a Tier 4 tailoring house operating out of the GLMZ upper commercial district, known for structured suiting and outerwear that signals corporate authority without ostentation. The Longline Overcoat is their flagship outerwear piece — a knee-length coat in heavyweight boiled wool or cashmere-wool blend, single-breasted with a notched lapel, slash pockets, and a back vent that allows for comfortable stride. The lining is a silk-weave in a subtle houndstooth. Offered in charcoal, camel, and an almost-black midnight navy.

This is the coat of senior analysts, department heads, and corponation liaisons who walk into rooms and need to be read immediately as someone of consequence. It is not showy. It does not need to be. The cut is authoritative, the fabric drapes with the weight of expensive things, and it holds a press through an entire workday. No tech features — Halversen's position is that tech is for people who cannot afford to simply look correct.
materials: boiled wool or cashmere-wool blend shell
what_it_says: You are someone who makes decisions that affect other people's lives and you dress accordingly. The coat is not a costume — it is the correct uniform for what you actually are.
story_hooks: A Halversen overcoat is found folded neatly over a chair in an abandoned Tier 4 office — no sign of the owner, no indication of why they left it behind
A Tier 2 character acquires a Halversen second-hand and finds that doors open differently when they wear it into certain buildings
Halversen keeps records of every coat they have made; a character needs to trace who owned a specific coat without alerting the tailoring house
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions ChemoShield BX-2 Dermal Toxin Barrier Implant

physical_description.visual_profile: A commanding knee-length silhouette that reads as institutional authority — structured shoulders, clean lines, substantial presence without aggression. Moves with deliberate weight and drape. The cut suggests someone who enters meetings, not someone who attends them.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not tight — allows for layered augmentation or subcutaneous tech beneath without disruption. Shoulders are slightly broad and squared. Sleeves taper cleanly to the wrist. The body skims without clinging. Back vent permits full stride without pulling.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight boiled wool or cashmere-wool blend — dense enough to hold shape through a full workday, luxurious enough to signal Tier 2-3 purchasing power from across a room.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost imperceptibly napped surface with subtle lustre. Fabric has weight that's tactile — substantial without being rough. Interior silk-weave lining in houndstooth adds whisper-soft texture where it matters.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal, camel, or midnight navy — all in tones that absorb light rather than reflect it. No patterns. The houndstooth lining is visible only when the coat moves or is removed, a quiet signal of investment.
physical_description.closures: Single-breasted with horn or bone buttons — traditional, reliable, corporate-coded. No zippers, no mag-snaps. The slowness of buttoning is intentional.
distinctive_features: Notched lapel in the classical Halversen cut
Slash pockets positioned for hand access without breaking silhouette
Back vent — single or double depending on variant
Silk houndstooth lining visible at cuffs and collar
Subtle interior branding at chest seam only
Finished hems that hold crease through repeated wear
No tech integration whatsoever — a statement in itself
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 corporate. Too expensive for working-class affectation, too restrained for Tier 1 ostentatious wealth. The price point and zero-tech philosophy place it firmly in the mid-executive zone.
physical_description.cultural_context: Corporate, specifically — department heads, senior analysts, corpo liaisons, risk managers, and anyone whose authority must be read in a single glance. The wearer is someone established enough not to need chrome, labels, or integrated displays. Wearing Halversen signals: 'I was approved for this, and I can afford to keep it pristine.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new, developing a broken-in patina over months of wear — subtle shine at lapels and cuffs, a deepening of fold-lines, eventual micro-pilling that only the wearer will notice. Cleaning is deliberate and infrequent.
